title: Super source follower
description: A super source follower (SSF): a plain source follower whose output resistance is driven down by a local feedback device. The input follower sets the DC level shift (the output sits about one input $V_{GS}$ below the input), and the feedback device senses the follower current and closes a local loop that lowers the output resistance by the loop gain $g_{m,fb}/g_{ds,in}$ (the feedback transconductance into the follower's own output resistance): $R_{out} \approx g_{ds,in}/((g_{m,in} + g_{mb,in}) * g_{m,fb})$, versus $1/g_{m,in}$ for a plain follower. The two devices share one branch: the input device's source is the output, the feedback device sits between the output and ground, and the feedback device's gate is the input device's drain. So the input device's drain-source voltage is not a free choice — it is the feedback device's gate-source voltage minus the output level. That makes it a compact low-impedance buffer. The feedback is a local loop; its own phase margin (whether that loop is stable) is a small-signal AC check the simulator owns, out of this sheet's scope — this sheet sizes the DC operating point and the low-frequency output resistance only. On the demo NMOS table both devices size against the same data.

params.name: I_in
params.note: current through the input follower device (held fixed by the bias source, which linearizes the buffer)

params.name: gm_id_fb
params.note: feedback device inversion: at fixed I_fb it sets gm_fb, and with it the loop gain gm_fb/gds_in

params.name: L_fb
params.note: the loop gain gm_fb/gds_in does not depend on L_fb (gm_fb is set by gm_id_fb and I_fb), so this knob moves the feedback device's vdsat and area, not Rout

params.name: vds_fb
params.note: feedback-device drain-source, which is the output node: the feedback device sits between the output and ground. Stated at this design point. Where the design is held fixed, the input device's gate (this node plus its gate-source voltage) is what stays put and the node is re-solved under it, between min and max.

doc.title: Feedback device
doc.description: The local-feedback device that senses the follower current; its transconductance into the follower's output resistance, gm_fb/gds_in, is the loop gain that lowers the output resistance.

doc.title: Input follower device
doc.description: The source-follower input device carrying a fixed current; its gm sets the base output resistance and its vgs the DC level shift.

equations.name: vds_in
equations.note: input-device drain-source: its drain sits on the feedback device's gate, one feedback gate-source voltage above ground, and its source is the output

equations.name: gm_in
equations.note: input follower transconductance (sets the plain-follower output resistance 1/gm_in)

equations.name: av0_fb
equations.note: reference reading of the feedback device's own intrinsic gain; the loop gain that Rout actually divides by is gm_fb/gds_in, not this

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: SSF output resistance: the local loop drives the follower's own output conductance down by the product of the two transconductances. The gds is the INPUT device's — it is the input device whose drain current the loop senses — and the source-body generator adds to gm because the output node is the input device's source. On a sky130 tt realization of this buffer this form lands within 3% of the measured 56 ohm

equations.name: Rout_plain
equations.note: the plain source-follower output resistance, for comparison

equations.name: level_shift
equations.note: output sits about one input Vgs below the input (source-follower DC level shift)

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents, taken as the input device's whole gate capacitance. It OVERSTATES what a driver sees — the source follows the gate near unity, bootstrapping most of the gate-source capacitance away. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — ONE stacked branch: the feedback device reuses the input device's current rather than drawing its own, so the supply pays for it once. A realization that biases the output node with a source of its own adds that current on top. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

checks.note: the buffer output resistance meets the target
